title: Wave 1 — Foundations
description: The eight architectural foundations almost every other issue is blocked on. Each is cheap now and expensive later. Executor interface (#1), session log (#2), contribution registries (#3), workflow model (#5), task-repository join (#7), agent catalog (#10), per-turn usage capture (#14), external MCP (#16). See #109.

title: Wave 2 — What the foundations unlock
description: The work that becomes possible, or merely cheap, once Wave 1 lands: ACP client (#58), executor profile config (#73), task dependencies (#6), sub-tasks (#56), GitHub integration (#15), single-command launcher (#17), panel layout (#11), MCP workspace discovery (#82).

title: Wave 3 — Capability breadth
description: Where the parity gap against comparable tools is widest: Docker (#96) and SSH (#97) executors, CLI passthrough (#59), MCP task creation (#99), push and pull-request integration (#71), notifications (#92), analytics (#91), multi-branch tasks (#57).

title: Wave 4 — The rest
description: Everything else, ordered by the priority labels rather than by wave. Populated automatically: any open issue not claimed by an earlier wave lands here.
